cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: A Kinder Version
cards.instruction: Protect someone from the full truth by offering a carefully edited explanation that feels kinder than complete honesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll find another exhibition for your portrait. The gallery thinks it needs a more adventurous room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're showing a fridge full of teeth. What did they say about mine?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll send a note about the sitter with it. They couldn't immediately tell who the face was meant to be.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's you. They called it unrecognisable, didn't they?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Knowing me would help. I'll stand beside the portrait in a matching shirt.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 leads finding another venue with softened feedback; A3 supplies sitter context instead of harsh judgment; A5 offers matching presence after B identifies A as sitter, protecting B through practical help.

responseLogic.evidence: A1 now identifies the gallery and A5 names the portrait and matching shirt; no visible but unnamed shirt is needed to understand the proposed recognition aid.

relationship.evidence: B2 challenges the adventurous explanation using the gallery current exhibit and B4 asks whether the real criticism was unrecognizability.

heightening.evidence: B4 identifying A as sitter causes A5 to stand with the portrait as context rather than confirm the full insult.
